title: Your First Platformer Game
description: Build a complete 2D side-scrolling platformer with running, jumping, sprite animations, collectible pickups, melee attacks, and enemy mobs.

blocks.content: In this tutorial, you will build a 2D platformer level in about **25 minutes**. Your player character will run, jump across platforms, collect animated coins, and fight patrolling enemy mobs with melee combos.

items.title: Responsive Controls
items.desc: Run, jump with variable height, and chain air or wall jumps using **Platformer Controller**.

items.title: State Animations
items.desc: Switch automatically between idle, run, jump, and fall sprite clips.

items.title: Collectible Pickups
items.desc: Add floating coins that increment your score and play sound effects on touch.

items.title: Combat & Enemy Mobs
items.desc: Swing frame-synced melee hitboxes against patrolling and chasing enemies.

blocks.content: Complete [Quick Start](getting_started/quick_start) first so you know how to create a project and navigate the workspace. Prepare a character spritesheet (idle, run, jump, fall, and attack frames) and a coin sprite in the **Assets** dock.

rows: Applies gravity to the player, solid blocking to platforms, and sensor detection to coins.
Renders character sprites and plays frame-by-frame animation clips.
Drives horizontal running, jump physics, and automatic animation switching.
Handles coin collection, player melee hitboxes, and enemy combat AI.

blocks.content: Start by placing solid ground platforms and configuring the player entity in the [Scene Hierarchy](interface/scene_hierarchy) and [Scene Viewport](interface/scene_viewport).

items: In the **Scene Hierarchy**, create an entity named **Ground** on your world layer and add [Shape Renderer](components/renderers/shape_renderer) (or [Tilemap](components/renderers/tilemap)), [Physics Body](components/physics_body), and [Multi-Collider](components/multi_collider).
In the [Property Inspector](interface/property_inspector), set **Ground**'s **Physics Body** **Body Type** to **Static** so it stays fixed in place.
Duplicate **Ground** (**Ctrl + D**) to arrange several elevated platforms and sloped ramps across the level.
Create a new entity named **Player**, set its **Tag** in the **Property Inspector** header to **player**, and position it above the starting platform.
Add [Image Renderer](components/renderers/sprite_renderer), [Sprite Animator](components/sprite_animator), **Physics Body**, and **Multi-Collider** to **Player**.
Set **Player**'s **Physics Body** **Body Type** to **Dynamic**, enable **Fixed Rotation**, and define **idle**, **run**, **jump**, **fall**, and **attack** clips inside **Sprite Animator**.

blocks.content: Next, wire a visual script on **Player** to process keyboard movement, animate the sprite, and lock the camera onto the character.

items: Select **Player**, click **Add Component** in the [Property Inspector](interface/property_inspector), and attach a [Script Controller](components/script_controller).
Create a new script named **PlayerLogic** and open it in the [Graph & Node Concepts](visual_scripting/graph_concepts) editor.
Add [On Tick](node_library/game_lifecycle#node-eventTick) and connect its execution and **deltaTime** outputs to [Platformer Controller](node_library/helper_tool#node-platformerController).
Set **Speed** to **220**, **Jump Force** to **450**, and **Coyote Time** to **0.1** on **Platformer Controller**.

Add [Platformer Animator](node_library/helper_tool#node-platformerAnimator) after **Platformer Controller** and wire **isMoving**, **isGrounded**, **isJumping**, and **isFalling** between the two nodes.

Add [On Scene Start](node_library/game_lifecycle#node-eventSceneStart) and connect it to [Camera Follow](node_library/game_renderer#node-actionCameraFollow) with **Smoothing** set to **0.12** so the viewport tracks **Player**.

blocks.content: Create floating coins that the player can pick up to increase their score.

items: Create a **Coin** entity in the [Scene Hierarchy](interface/scene_hierarchy) and attach [Image Renderer](components/renderers/sprite_renderer), [Physics Body](components/physics_body) (**Static**), [Multi-Collider](components/multi_collider), and [Script Controller](components/script_controller).
In **Coin**'s **Multi-Collider**, enable **Is Sensor** so the player runs through the coin without physical blocking.
Open **Coin**'s script graph and wire [On Tick](node_library/game_lifecycle#node-eventTick) into [Collectable Item](node_library/helper_tool#node-collectableItem).
On **Collectable Item**, set **Collector Tag** to **player**, **Score Value** to **10**, **Despawn Action** to **destroy**, and **Auto Bobbing** to **true**.
Drag **Coin** into the **Assets** dock to save it as a reusable [Prefab](components/entities_and_prefabs), then place several coin instances across your platforms.

blocks.content: Now add melee combat to the player and create an enemy mob that patrols a platform and chases the player when nearby.

items: In **PlayerLogic**, add [Platformer Combat](node_library/helper_tool#node-platformerCombat) after [Platformer Controller](node_library/helper_tool#node-platformerController), set **Target Tag** to **enemy**, and set **Attack Key** to **j**.
Wire **facingDirection** and **isGrounded** from **Platformer Controller** into **Platformer Combat** so the attack hitbox spawns in front of the player.
Connect the **On Hit** output of **Platformer Combat** to [Shake Transform](node_library/game_animation#node-actionShakeTransform) for impact feedback when a strike lands.

Create an **Enemy** entity in the [Scene Hierarchy](interface/scene_hierarchy), set its **Tag** to **enemy**, and attach [Image Renderer](components/renderers/sprite_renderer), [Sprite Animator](components/sprite_animator), [Physics Body](components/physics_body) (**Dynamic**, **Fixed Rotation**), [Multi-Collider](components/multi_collider), and [Script Controller](components/script_controller).

In **Enemy**'s script graph, wire [On Tick](node_library/game_lifecycle#node-eventTick) into [Ping-Pong Stepper](node_library/helper_tool#node-pingPongStepper) for platform patrolling, or into [Enemy Chaser](node_library/helper_tool#node-enemyChaser) and [Enemy Combat](node_library/helper_tool#node-enemyCombat) with **Target Entity** set to **player**.

blocks.content: Run the live preview in the editor to test your platformer mechanics.

items: Click **Play** in the top bar to start the simulation.
Use **A** and **D** to run across platforms and press **W** or **Space** to jump.
Run through your **Coin** instances to verify that they bob, trigger collection events, and despawn on contact.
Approach the **Enemy** mob and press **J** to swing your melee attack and defeat it, then click **Stop** and press **Ctrl + S** to save.

blocks.message: Turn on collider wireframes in **Project Settings** under **Debugging** if you want to inspect your melee attack hitbox bounds while testing.

blocks.content: You can download two ready-to-play **.lupisproject** sample archives for this tutorial: one focused on platforming and collectible pickups, and one featuring the melee attack combo system and enemy mobs.

rows: Player movement, multi-level platforms, animated bobbing coins, pickup sound effects, and a live score HUD.
Player melee attack combos, active frame hitboxes, knockback, and patrolling/chasing enemy mobs.

items: Click either download link in the table above to save the **.lupisproject** file to your computer.
Open the **My Projects** dashboard in Lupis Engine (see [Project & Export](getting_started/project_and_export#manage-projects)).
Drag and drop the downloaded **.lupisproject** file anywhere onto the dashboard, or click **Load Project** and choose the file.
Click the imported project card to open it in the editor, then click **Play** in the top bar to playtest the game.
